send.needSeed: This device doesn't hold this wallet's key yet. Enter your recovery phrase once to unlock sending here.
send.wrongSeed: That seed belongs to a different wallet — it does not unlock this one. Check which wallet you are restoring, or switch to the wallet that seed belongs to.
send.partialRecorded: {{message}} The part already broadcast is recorded in History.
send.manyNotes: Your balance sits in {{n}} notes. If this amount cannot fit in one transaction, nothing is sent and the wallet will offer consolidation or an explicit split payment.
send.memoSealed: “{{memo}}” — encrypted inside the payment; only the recipient can read it.
send.warmingNote: ⚡ This first payment will take a few minutes — the wallet has to locate your coins in the chain before it can spend them. It only does this once; later payments take seconds.
send.signedOnDevice: Verified and signed on your device, then broadcast. Usually takes a few seconds.
send.chooseSafely: Choose safely: consolidation is recommended. “Send in parts” broadcasts independent transactions; accepted parts cannot be automatically reversed if a later part fails.
send.consolidationSentBody: Wait for the new note to mature, then retry the full payment.
send.splitProgress: Your balance is spread across many small notes, so this payment is being sent as {{parts}} transactions — {{sent}} of {{total}} ZKAS confirmed so far. Keep this page open until it finishes.
send.title: Send
send.clipboardEmptyBody: Copy the address first, then tap Paste.
send.clipboardBlockedTitle: This browser won't share the clipboard
send.clipboardBlockedBody: Press and hold the address field, then choose Paste.
send.badAddress: That doesn't look like a zkas: address.
send.selfAddress: That's your own address. The payment works — it just returns to you, minus the fee.
send.feeHint: Leave empty and the wallet picks the fee. Raise it only after a fee error.
send.memoHint: Encrypted inside the payment — only the recipient can read it. Never appears on-chain or on the explorer.
send.maturingHint: Only {{spendable}} is ready to spend right now — {{maturing}} is still arriving. Coins become spendable about 10 minutes after they land, including the change from a payment you just made. It'll be ready shortly.
send.notEnough: Not enough funds: {{spendable}} spendable, need {{need}} incl. up to {{maxFee}} fee.
send.feeSummary: + {{min}}–{{max}} fee (scales with how many coins get combined) = up to {{total}} total
send.catchingUp: Still catching up with the chain — you can pay once it finishes, so the wallet knows about all your coins.
send.warmBanner:
⚡ Your first payment will take a few minutes.
Locating your coins — this happens once. You can start the payment now.

sign.title: Sign message
sign.intro: Prove you control this wallet's address without spending. The signature discloses your viewing key (enables note detection, never spend authority).
sign.fvkWarning: Signing hands the verifier your viewing key: from then on they can see this wallet's balance, its history and where you send. If that matters, sign from a separate wallet — you can add one in Settings.

verify.title: Verify message
verify.intro: Runs entirely in your browser — no server involved.
verify.reasonMismatch: signature does not verify for this address/message
verify.valid: ✓ VALID — the signer controls this address.

history.title: History
history.recovering: Recovering your history from the chain — a minute or two. You can leave this tab.
history.empty: Nothing yet. Payments you receive and send show up here.
history.sentPrivately: Sent privately. Watch it confirm below — this updates live.
history.held_one: {{count}} outgoing transaction in flight — {{amount}} ZKAS temporarily held until it confirms (returned automatically within ~1 hour if it never does).
history.held_other: {{count}} outgoing transactions in flight — {{amount}} ZKAS temporarily held until it confirms (returned automatically within ~1 hour if it never does).
history.rescanHint: Re-read the chain to rebuild this history and recover any funds the local view lost.
history.recoveredNote: Recovered from the chain by your viewing key. Tap a payment for details.
history.exportFailed: Could not export the CSV on this device.

daemonSetting.unreachable: Couldn't reach a wallet service at {{url}} ({{detail}}). Make sure zkas-walletd is running there and the port is open. Nothing was changed — still using {{current}}.
daemonSetting.title: Connect to your own node
daemonSetting.intro: Your seed always signs on this device. But the hosted service still sees your viewing key — it can watch your balance, your history and where you send. To keep even that private, run zkas-walletd on your own node and connect this wallet straight to it.
daemonSetting.enterIp: Just enter your node's IP address — we add the rest.
daemonSetting.nativeTransports: The installed app supports HTTPS and plain HTTP LAN connections.
daemonSetting.webTransports: The web wallet requires HTTPS; use the installed app for plain HTTP on a LAN.
daemonSetting.portNote: Uses port {{port}} by default — add :port only if you changed it.

vaultSetting.title: Security & backup
vaultSetting.plaintextWarning: This wallet's seed is stored unencrypted on this computer — anyone who copies the file can spend your funds. Set a passphrase to encrypt it; your balance and history are untouched.
vaultSetting.lockingNote: Locking stops the daemon and forgets your passphrase until you re-enter it.
vaultSetting.lockBody: The wallet daemon stops and your passphrase is forgotten. You will need it again to unlock. Your funds are not affected.

autoConsolidationCard.title: Automatic consolidation
autoConsolidationCard.intro: Occasionally merges your oldest notes in the background so a payment always fits. Each merge costs a small fee — turn it off to merge yourself with Consolidate instead.
autoConsolidationCard.offNote: Off. A large payment may need splitting until you merge with Consolidate.

debugLogsCard.title: Debug logs
debugLogsCard.verboseHint: More detail from the on-device engine. Turn on when a wallet is stuck opening or a send fails, then Show engine logs.
debugLogsCard.noLogs: No logs yet — the engine may not be running.

networkPrivacyCard.title: Network privacy
networkPrivacyCard.desktopNote: Keys stay in this app. Strongest privacy: run your own node (Node page). You can also connect over Tor if Tor is running on this computer — both from Chain source above.
networkPrivacyCard.enterAddress: Enter a wallet-service address (host:port or an .onion).
networkPrivacyCard.intro: What your wallet connects to. Tap to switch.
networkPrivacyCard.publicHint: Fast. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
networkPrivacyCard.torHint: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
networkPrivacyCard.customHint: A wallet daemon you run yourself.

backgroundSyncCard.title: Background sync
backgroundSyncCard.intro: While on, the phone wakes about every 15 min (even closed) to stay synced and notify you of payments. Off, it catches up when you open the app. The seed stays on this device either way.
backgroundSyncCard.onNote: On. Android may delay the wake when the battery is low — payments are never lost, the notification is simply later.

biometricToggle.linkIntroPin: Enter your current PIN once to link it to this device's fingerprint. It stays sealed on the device; the fingerprint only releases it to open the app.
biometricToggle.linkIntroPassphrase: Enter your current passphrase once to link it to this device's fingerprint. It stays sealed on the device; the fingerprint only releases it to open the app.
biometricToggle.isOn: Fingerprint unlock is on. Open the app with a fingerprint instead of typing.
biometricToggle.offerPin: Unlock with a fingerprint instead of typing your PIN.
biometricToggle.offerPassphrase: Unlock with a fingerprint instead of typing your passphrase.

appLockSetting.mismatch: The two entries do not match.
appLockSetting.wrongSecret: That passphrase does not unlock this device.
appLockSetting.title: App lock
appLockSetting.enableIntro: Choose what to unlock with. This encrypts the key of every wallet on this device and asks for it when the app opens — while locked, this device holds nothing that can spend any of them.
appLockSetting.alsoBioPin: Also unlock with fingerprint (you'll scan it once to link). Your PIN keeps working.
appLockSetting.alsoBioPassphrase: Also unlock with fingerprint (you'll scan it once to link). Your passphrase keeps working.
appLockSetting.backupFirstPin: Back up your wallet first. Nothing stores this PIN, so if you forget it the only way back in is your seed phrase or a backup file.
appLockSetting.backupFirstPassphrase: Back up your wallet first. Nothing stores this passphrase, so if you forget it the only way back in is your seed phrase or a backup file.
appLockSetting.pinStrength: A PIN stops someone who picks up your phone. Use a passphrase for stronger protection.
appLockSetting.disableIntroPin: Enter your current PIN to turn the lock off. Your key will be stored unencrypted on this device again.
appLockSetting.disableIntroPassphrase: Enter your current passphrase to turn the lock off. Your key will be stored unencrypted on this device again.
appLockSetting.onNotePin: On. Every wallet's key on this device is encrypted, and the app asks for your PIN to open. It re-locks itself after a few minutes in the background.
appLockSetting.onNotePassphrase: On. Every wallet's key on this device is encrypted, and the app asks for your passphrase to open. It re-locks itself after a few minutes in the background.
appLockSetting.offIntro: Your wallet keys are stored on this device unencrypted. Turn on a PIN or passphrase and every one of them is encrypted at rest, and the app asks for it on open — so someone holding this device, or a backup of its data, cannot spend from it.

switchWallet.title: Wallets
switchWallet.intro: This device can hold several wallets at once. Switching between them keeps every one of them — their keys, history and contacts stay exactly where they are.
switchWallet.removeBody: This wallet's key and data are erased from this device. Your other wallets are not affected. The coins stay on-chain but are unreachable from here without a backup or seed phrase.

deviceSeedBackup.noKey: This device holds no spending key for the wallet — it can watch the balance but not spend. Restore your seed phrase on the Send tab to spend from here.
deviceSeedBackup.mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
deviceSeedBackup.copied: Your backup is copied. Paste it somewhere safe now — a password manager or a note to yourself.
deviceSeedBackup.written: Backup written. Keep it off this computer. It is encrypted, useless without the passphrase.
deviceSeedBackup.intro: Back up your wallet. Save an encrypted copy so you can restore this wallet if the machine is lost.
deviceSeedBackup.loseWarning: Lose the backup passphrase and the file cannot be opened — not by us, not by anyone. Your seed phrase remains the other way back in.

restoreSeedBackup.wrongWallet: That backup belongs to a different wallet than the one open now, so it was not applied — restoring it here would overwrite this wallet's key. Use “Add separate wallet”, then restore the backup there.
restoreSeedBackup.storeFailed: This device could not store the wallet key — free up space and try again.
restoreSeedBackup.restored: Wallet restored. Your balance rebuilds from the chain — this takes a minute or two.
restoreSeedBackup.intro: Restore from backup. Open an encrypted backup file and put its wallet on this computer.
restoreSeedBackup.passPlaceholder: The passphrase you gave the file

backupWallet.mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
backupWallet.written: Backup written. Keep it off this computer — a USB stick or password manager. It is encrypted.
backupWallet.intro: Backup — save an encrypted copy of your wallet to a file. Restore it on any computer with this app. Give it its own passphrase; do not reuse the one that unlocks this device.
backupWallet.loseWarning: Lose this passphrase and the file cannot be opened — not by us, not by anyone. Your seed phrase remains the other way back in.

nodeSourceSetting.title: Wallet node
nodeSourceSetting.intro: The embedded wallet engine keeps your keys on this computer. Node changes are checked before the wallet switches.

desktopEngineDown.startingTitle: Starting the wallet on this computer
desktopEngineDown.startingBody: Loading your wallet and catching up to the chain. The first run takes a few minutes; it keeps going if you close this.
desktopEngineDown.lostTitle: Lost the connection to the wallet on this computer
desktopEngineDown.notStartedTitle: The wallet on this computer didn't start
desktopEngineDown.lostBody: The wallet is running on this computer but stopped answering. Retry reconnects to it.
desktopEngineDown.notStartedBody: The wallet that runs on this computer isn't answering. Your coins are safe on the chain — this is only how the app is reading them.
desktopEngineDown.publicHint: You can use the public wallet service instead: it has already scanned the chain, so nothing has to start or sync here.
desktopEngineDown.retryHint: If retrying does not help, the public wallet service above needs nothing running on this computer. You can switch back to running it here later, from Chain source.

setup.title: Can't reach the wallet service
setup.nativeDown: The wallet service isn't responding. Check your connection and try again shortly — your funds are safe on-chain.
setup.hostedDown: The hosted wallet service isn't responding. Nothing for you to run — try again shortly.
setup.privacyNote: Your spending key is on this device either way — it is never sent to the service. What running your own zkas-walletd changes is privacy: the hosted service can see which wallet is asking about which blocks, and your own daemon sees only what you already know.
setup.nativeTransports: The installed app accepts HTTPS and plain HTTP LAN addresses.
setup.webTransports: The web wallet requires an HTTPS wallet-service URL.

privateSends.intro: Your payments normally carry a copy of their details encrypted to your own key, so your history survives a restore and you can prove a payment later. Private sends leave that copy out.
privateSends.cost: The cost is permanent: a private send cannot be recovered after you restore this wallet, cannot be shown in history on another device, and cannot be proven to anyone. The recipient still receives it normally.
